title: Drug Liquid Imaging
author: Ida Barlow
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfgujjww

steps.title: Prepare worm culture 4 days prior
steps.instruction: Four days before the experiment, transfer six N2 adult gravid worms from a maintenance plate to a new 60 mm NGM plate containing OP50; this yields approximately 100 L4 worms by the morning of day 3 (≈00:30:00 for the transfer).

steps.title: Identify and label drugs
steps.instruction: Identify the drugs to be used and verify that each is correctly labelled and handled.

steps.title: Calculate compound amounts
steps.instruction: Calculate the weight and solvent volume needed for the desired final concentration (for powdered compounds) or the dilution factor (for liquid compounds); make all calculations 1000‑fold higher than the final plate concentration (e.g., prepare a mM stock for a µM final concentration).

steps.title: Prepare drug solution
steps.instruction: In a fume hood, weigh the calculated amount of compound into a labeled Eppendorf tube, add the calculated volume of solvent (e.g., DMSO), close the tube, then vortex at speed 10 for 30 seconds (repeat longer if needed) until the compound is fully dissolved.

steps.title: Select and inspect agar plates
steps.instruction: Choose fresh, unseeded 35 mm NGM plates no older than 3 days; inspect each for an even agar surface (uneven agar can cause blurry images and affect drug concentration).

steps.title: Label plates
steps.instruction: Label the side of each plate with the compound name, concentration, and date.

steps.title: Apply water and drug to plates
steps.instruction: In a flow hood, pipette 50 µL sterile water onto the centre of each agar plate, then, before it dries, add 3.5 µL of the prepared compound solution (verify correct compound and concentration).

steps.title: Dry plates
steps.instruction: Leave the plates in the flow hood with lids off for approximately 30 minutes until the liquid dries.

steps.title: Seed plates with OP50
steps.instruction: Take a Falcon tube of OP50 from the fridge, vortex at speed 10 until no pellet remains, dilute 1:10 in M9 solution, then pipette 50 µL of this diluted OP50 onto the centre of each dried drug plate; if some plates dry earlier, replace lids to prevent overdrying.

steps.title: Incubate plates overnight
steps.instruction: Leave the seeded plates at room temperature in the dark overnight.

steps.title: Label plates for imaging
steps.instruction: Using the experimental Excel template, label each plate with its set number and rig position; add a black‑dot annotation to half of the plates as indicated.

steps.title: Transfer worms onto drug plates
steps.instruction: From synchronized worm stocks, pick 10 worms onto each drug plate; complete each set within 10 minutes to maintain equivalence.

steps.title: Prepare liquid assay chambers
steps.instruction: After 3 h 45 min, set up the liquid assay chambers for the set by adding 30 µL of the corresponding compound diluted to the desired µM concentration.

steps.title: Move worms to liquid chambers
steps.instruction: Pick 5 worms from each solid drug plate into the corresponding liquid assay chamber, immediately place the second coverslip (touch one side of the tape and let it drop from a minimal height) to minimise bubbles and leakage, and image immediately (no acclimation).

steps.title: Place chambers on imaging rig
steps.instruction: Place the liquid assay chambers onto the correct rig positions; start the experiment (init_exp) which creates folders on each Windows 10 PC.

steps.title: Acquire images
steps.instruction: Record images for 15 minutes at 25 fps, saving the data in .hdf5 format.

steps.title: Transfer data to server
steps.instruction: Copy the .hdf5 files from each PC to the central server.

description: NOTES: To increase the number of worms needed simply increase the number of plates that are produced in step 1. b.For drug experiments need 10 worms for each drug for each dose in triplicate (so 10*3*3 worms) – one plate per drug
